newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed lower on Friday, with another fall on Wall Street and a weak Dutch bond market seen as signals to take profits after a week which had seen the AEX index advance around 20 points.
"We've seen selling on Wall Street's fall today and yesterday and a lower bond market," said a dealer. "People are taking profits after the rally we've seen this week."

The AEX share index closed 10.54 points or 1.38 percent lower at 752.62. Dealers said the index could be heading for a near-term trading range of 720 to 760 as sentiment fluctuates ahead of a definitive steer on the direction of interest rates.
Dealers said yesterday's Wall Street performance was all the more disappointing because it masked an eight percent leap by IBM in the wake of its first quarter results announcement.

"If you excluded IBM, the Dow would have been a lot lower," said a dealer. "Now you see that most results are out people in the States are looking back to other problems that might affect the market. Will the Fed do anything about interest rates in May or not?" he said.
Markets around the world wobbled a few weeks ago after U.S. economic data suggested the Fed's 25 basis point interest rate hike at the end of March might be followed by another in May.
"I think the closer we get to the FOMC meeting in May the more anxious we will get about interest rates," he added.

"People are still worried about interest rates," said another dealer, adding rate concerns this week had subsided somewhat because little fresh information had emerged about the state of the U.S. economy.

"The market will be more nervous next week because we will get more economic figures and this will give direction to the market one way or the other. My feeling is that the market is more likely to move downwards," he said.
Shares in chemicals company Akzo dropped 9.70 guilders to 262.00 after reporting a 2.4 percent rise in first quarter net profit to 340 million guilders.
The figure came at the lower end of a 322-380 million guilder range and wiped out the share's 10.00 guilder rise from a week ago on optimism ahead of the results.

Philips was the only stock to hold its ground on a sharply lower leader board, ending unchanged at 98.50 guilders as more analysts upgraded the stock after Wednesday's results. Elsewhere losses ranged to 5.50 guilders as in Unilever at 372.30, while Oce van der Grinten fell 4.30 guilders to 234.00. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
